desc: Formalize the greedy absorption process as interval expansion and prove that absorbing any strictly smaller neighbor is always safe (exchange argument).
Compute prefix sums P[0..N] so any interval sum is O(1).
Design O(N) monotonic-stack precomputation of R_bound (right-only reach) and L_bound (left-only reach) using prefix-sum stopping conditions.
Design per-K two-directional block-jump simulation using R_bound/L_bound to reach the fixpoint interval and derive B_K.
Implement solve() reading stdin, running the algorithm, and printing B_1..B_N space-separated.
Verify correctness on both samples by hand-trace of the stack precomputation and per-K simulation.
Stress-test against a brute-force O(N^2) simulator on small random arrays (including equal elements, monotone, and all-ones cases) to confirm correctness and strict-inequality edge cases.
Prove or stress-test the amortized total complexity of the per-K jumping loop; confirmed it is O(N²) worst-case with concrete counterexample.

Replace the O(N²) per-K jumping loop with a divide-and-conquer O(N log N) algorithm: recursively solve left/right halves, then compute cross-boundary expansions for each K using two pointers and prefix sums.
